name: vim-big-cmdline
description: A large, bottom-screen command/search input for VSCodeVim, with substitute regex highlighting.

commands.title: Vim Big Cmdline: Clear Command History

vimBigCmdline.fontSize.description: Font size, in pixels, for the Vim command line. 0 (the default) follows your editor font size and adds 15%, so the command line reads a little larger than the editor without becoming a display font. Set a number to pin it; smaller values fit more of a long command on one line.

vimBigCmdline.fontFamily.description: CSS font-family used in the large Vim command line.

vimBigCmdline.panelHeightHint.description: Minimum height, in pixels, for the input box. The input already fills the whole sidebar, so this only matters when the view is somewhere short.

vimBigCmdline.wrapLongInput.description: Wrap long commands onto multiple lines instead of scrolling horizontally on one line.

enumDescriptions: Follow VSCodeVim's vim.ignorecase and vim.smartcase settings (both default to true, so matching is case-insensitive until the pattern contains an uppercase letter — including one inside an escape such as \S, which is how VSCodeVim tests it).
Always ignore case in the preview.
Always match case in the preview.
vimBigCmdline.caseSensitivity.description: How the live preview treats letter case. Inline \c and \C in the pattern always win over this setting.

enumDescriptions: Translate patterns the way VSCodeVim does: JavaScript regex syntax, so ( ) group and + ? | { } work unescaped, plus VSCodeVim's escapes (\c, \C, \<, \>, \n, \x, \h, \a, \l, \u and so on). Note that \( and \+ are literal characters here, as they are in VSCodeVim.
Interpret patterns as plain JavaScript regular expressions, with no escape translation at all.
vimBigCmdline.regexFlavor.description: Regex dialect used for the live preview. This only affects the preview; VSCodeVim always executes the command itself.

vimBigCmdline.restoreSidebarWhenDone.description: When you press Enter or Esc, hand the sidebar back to the view named by vimBigCmdline.restoreSidebarCommand, so the command line shrinks to its activity bar icon. This only applies when opening the command line is what revealed it; if its view was already on screen, the sidebar is left alone.

vimBigCmdline.restoreSidebarCommand.description: Which view the sidebar goes back to when the command line closes. Use workbench.view.scm, workbench.view.search, or any other view command if you keep something else there — or workbench.action.closeSidebar to hide the sidebar entirely. Leave it empty to change nothing and keep the command line's view on screen in its idle state.

vimBigCmdline.executeWithVscodeVimRemap.description: Send completed input to VSCodeVim via vim.remap. Disable only for debugging.
